The path was sized for beings of Vex’thul’s scale, making Noah and Ozymandias look like insects following a giant.

"To be part of our tribe," Vex’thul explained as they walked, "you have to drink this Drop of Everything to ensure you won’t harm those here... well, even though you’re weaker than even the livestock we rear.
Haha!
Here you go."
The Early Creature tapped the air, and reality responded by producing two perfectly circular drops of multicolored glory.
They hung in space before Noah and Ozymandias, each one containing spectrums that shouldn’t exist in the same dimension.
Noah’s existence trembled at their proximity.
|Utterly unfathomable loot observed|
|What an effort to even perceive this!|
|What a harvest awaits!|
|Item: Drop of Everything - Verdant Eternia Tribe|
|Description: Concentrated Everything from the Verdant Eternia Tribe|
|One of the oldest Early Creature settlements in the First Folds|
|Effect upon consumption:|
|- Binds consumer to Verdant Eternia non-aggression pact
|- Prevents harm against other tribe members
|- Grants tribal marking and recognition
|- Immediate gain: +1,000,000,000,000 Complexity
|- Immediate gain: +1,000,000,000,000 Purity
|Warning: Binding is existentially permanent|
|Note: This is how Early Creatures traded power itself|
Oh!
Was that a trillion?
Was it truly?!
Oh!!!
Khor’s voice rang in his mind with fondness and memory.
"Drops of Everything.
The currency between Early Creatures that all others sought but could never replicate.
They were so powerful that they cultivated and traded...
Everythings themselves."
Her consciousness fragment pulsed with memory.
"Early Creatures learned to extract, condense, and crystallize Everythings into tradeable form.
A Drop might contain someone’s Everything of Joy, another’s Everything of Strength.

They would cultivate rare Everythings specifically to trade...growing them outwardly or within themselves like internal gardens, harvesting them when ripe, condensing them into Drops that could be consumed by others."

chapters.title: Chapter 4110: The First Leader! I
paragraphs: She paused, her tone growing more serious.

"The Verdant Eternia Tribe...I don’t remember much about them. But taking their Drop of Everything would mean they cannot harm you, and you cannot harm them. Such a thing would carry on permanently as if lets say you were to meet Early Creatures from the Verdant Eternia Tribe in your current age, which would be countless epochs and eons from now, neither they or you would be able to harm each other."
Khor said such words as Noah’s eyes became stern, but his eyes remained luminous!
He looked at the Drop floating before him, then decisively opened his mouth and swallowed it.
It was fucking 1 Trillion in Complexity and Purity. He was swallowing it!
HUUM!

The sensation defied description. It wasn’t taste or temperature or texture but something more fundamental....like swallowing a small Folds that immediately began unpacking itself throughout his existence.
It tasted like glory. It smelled like Quintessence! And it burned with fierce glory.
|Drop of Everything Consumed|
|First personal Everything consumption detected!|
|Principle of Perpetual Harvest recognizing MONUMENTAL effort|
|Rewards calculating...|
|Base gain from Drop: +1,000,000,000,000 Complexity|
|Base gain from Drop: +1,000,000,000,000 Purity|
|First consumption bonus: +250,000,000,000 to each|
|Perpetual Harvest pulses even further as it sits at 2% and increases the gains!|
|Final gains:|
|Complexity: +1,500,000,000,000(1.5 Trillion)|
He almost wanted to bellow and scream!

It was like brilliant fire coursed through him as the waves of complexity and purity painted his Atlas, His Towers of Osmont, his Heart, and everything else as everything...began to exponentially scale upwards.
|Verdant Eternia Tribal Binding: ACTIVE|
|You cannot harm tribe members|
|Tribe members cannot harm you|
|Access to tribal resources: GRANTED|
|Tribal marking manifesting...|
The Drop spread through his existence like liquid starlight, touching every aspect of his being.
Joy flooded through him...not artificial happiness but the simple pleasure of becoming more!
His first thought after the sensation settled was calculating: just how many of these Drops could he take from here?
Beside him, Ozymandias consumed his Drop with mechanical efficiency.
|Ozymandias - Drop of Everything consumed|
|Pure existence consuming pure Everything|
|Conversion at maximum efficiency|
|Tribal binding established through shared existence|
On both their foreheads, a verdant teardrop marking appeared...emerald green that shifted through every shade of life.
Noah noticed the same marking on Vex’thul’s massive forehead, though his contained additional patterns suggesting rank or achievement.
"Okay, Little Things Os and Ozy," Vex’thul said with satisfaction, "welcome to the Verdant Eternia Tribe. Come, let us see what tasks can be given to weak things like you..."
The casual dismissal of their power should have been insulting, but in context, it was simply accurate.
They were weak by the standards of beings who treated reality as suggestion. The question was how quickly that could change.

As they walked deeper into the village, Noah’s mind raced with possibilities. He had just gained 1.5 trillion in both Complexity and Purity from a single Drop...something given casually as an entrance fee. If this was their currency, their casual trade, what other treasures did this village hold?
The structures grew larger and more complex as they proceeded.

What had looked like simple stone age construction from afar revealed itself as incredibly sophisticated...buildings that existed in multiple dimensions simultaneously, forges where concepts were given physical form!

Early Creatures of various forms moved through the spaces. Some humanoid like Vex’thul, others abstract geometries that somehow radiated personality, a few that seemed to be living ideas that had decided to try having bodies.
All bore the verdant teardrop marking, all radiated power that made Noah’s trillion-level complexity feel quaint.

"The livestock pens are there," Vex’thul pointed to an area where creatures that would be apocalyptic threats in Noah’s era were casually grazing. "The youngling training grounds are there- you’re probably too weak to survive their play, so avoid that area."
Each casual revelation painted a picture of civilization that would terrify even Living Existences of his current age!

"The Drops of Everything are distributed daily at the Everflow," Vex’thul continued. "Though with your limited capacity, more than one per day would probably cause problems for you. The Tribe Elders might find use for you...they always need subjects for testing new Everything combinations."
Oh.
Subjects?
The glory and loot that had provided itself so far faded as the reminder came that in these Grounds, the mortality rate was unfathomably high!

The implications were also astonishing regarding the experiements. Daily distribution of Drops worth trillions in advancement. Elders experimenting with Everything combinations. A society where power was so abundant it was given away as daily rations.
Noah had found exactly what he needed...a place where twenty hours could transform him completely.
The question was whether he could survive the transformation!
As Vex’thul led them through the village’s main thoroughfare, the atmosphere suddenly shifted.
Temperature spiked without warning, and Noah felt his existence begin to burn...not his body, but the fundamental fact of his being.
A figure approached that redefined beauty through terror. Her obsidian skin seemed to drink light, while pure white flames danced around her form in patterns that suggested consciousness.
Each step she took left crystallized fire in the ground that would burn for eons.
|WARNING: Atmospheric damage detected|
|Early Creature’s passive aura causing existential combustion|
|Persevering requires IMMENSE effort|
|Survival attempt recognized by Perpetual Harvest|
|Effort reward calculated:|
|Complexity gained: +10,000,000,000 for every second of perseverance|
|Purity gained: +10,000,000,000 for every second of perseverance|
Oh?!
Noah gritted his teeth against the sensation of slowly ceasing to exist. How was this not considered harm? The tribal binding should have prevented-
"Sear’ya," Vex’thul called out with mild reproach, "if you don’t control your aura, you may just burn the new entrants."
The female Early Creature looked down at them with eyes that contained supernovas as she titled her head.
Her animal clothing seem royal and ancient at the same time as her hair danced crimson gold, and her voice was like a sharp blade of existence!
"None here can harm each other. Before any permanent damage occurs, my flames would automatically be reigned in."
As if demonstrating, her white flames swirled and retracted into her body, the temperature dropping from existentially lethal to merely uncomfortably warm.
She studied Noah and Ozymandias with obvious disdain. "Are all newly born Creatures becoming this weak now? They can barely withstand even ambient temperature."

chapters.title: Chapter 4111: The First Leader! II
paragraphs: Before Noah could respond, she turned her attention to Vex’thul, her expression growing serious.

"I just returned from the neighboring Ra’ni Tribe. Half their hunting parties have gone missing." She paused, white flames flickering with agitation. "The...First Leader, Gilgamesh, is expanding faster than we anticipated.
HUUM!
Vex’thul’s casual demeanor vanished. "Gilgamesh...is moving truly? I thought it was all rumors..."
Sear’ya replied, her voice carrying weight. "He’s offering something none can refuse...unlimited Drops of Everything. Not daily rations but continuous flow."
"How can he produce such quantities?" Vex’thul asked, his massive form tensing. "Even the eldest tribes can only...."

Sear’ya’s flames pulsed with uncertainty. "The rumors say he’s discovered something- a way to cultivate Everythings at accelerated rates. And there’s more..." She hesitated, as if speaking it would make it real. "They say THE Living Spirit stands beside him."
Vex’thul actually stepped back, his crystalline skin flickering with shock. "THE Living Spirit? That’s impossible. THE Living Existences don’t involve themselves in out matters."

"Yet witnesses from three different tribes report the same thing...a being of pure spiritual authority beside Gilgamesh, teaching him methods that shouldn’t exist yet." Her gaze grew distant. "If true, it explains everything. THE Living Spirit could show him how to mass-produce Everythings, how to bind loyalty through abundance rather than force."

She glanced at Noah and Ozymandias. "Keep your new pets close, Vex’thul. Gilgamesh has been recruiting the weak specifically- easier to elevate, more grateful for power, more loyal to their benefactor. These two would be perfect candidates for his growing coalition. Of course, there are rumors that others have to give their Blood in exchange for the chance to join them. If their blood is deemed not worthy...."
She never finished her words as she sighed.
With that cliffhanger, she departed in a pulse of white fire that left afterimages burned into reality.
Vex’thul stood still for long moments, his eyes focused on horizons beyond the village. "Move along," he finally told them, his earlier friendliness replaced by deep contemplation.
As they continued walking, Khor’s voice resonated in Noah’s mind with recognition that transcended surprise.
"Gilgamesh... now that’s a name that echoes through existence itself. He was the first Early Creature looked to as a leading force apart from THE Creature itself."
Her consciousness fragment pulsed with ancient memory.

"When Early Creatures first began organizing into groups, most operated through consensus or might. But Gilgamesh proposed something different...leadership through provision. Why fight when you could simply offer more than anyone else? Why conquer when beings would willingly follow whoever granted them the most power?"
Her tone grew more contemplative.

"He was called The First Leader because he was the first to understand that authority didn’t require force if you controlled the resources everyone needed. In your era, this may see obvious. But in the First Folds, when every being was essentially a terrifying force unto themselves, the idea of voluntary subordination in exchange for benefit was revolutionary."
She paused, processing the implications.
"I did not know that...the Living Spirit was involved here. THE Living Existences were supposed to be neutral, above the conflicts of Early Creatures in the beginning..."

Noah absorbed this information while following Vex’thul deeper into the village. A figure from the earliest myths of existence, potentially backed by one of THE Living Existences themselves, building an empire of Early Creatures.
Whatever happened to such a being?!

"The question," Khor mused, "is whether Gilgamesh’s vision of unified Early Creatures under his leadership is progression or catastrophe. Unity sounds positive until you realize it means everyone serves one will, one vision, one interpretation of what existence should become."
The words felt like a warning and lesson all at once!
Vex’thul’s crystalline form moved through the tribal pathways.
Each step left impressions in ground that had been compressed by eons of Early Creature passage, the very earth here denser than planets in Noah’s era.
The Pattern Keeper’s usual jovial demeanor had given way to contemplation that made the air around him taste of concern.

The village sprawled around them gloriously. Buildings carved from single stones that had witnessed the birth of concepts rose like monuments to what architecture could be when reality was merely a suggestion.
The path they walked was wide enough for beings of Vex’thul’s scale, which meant Noah and Ozymandias looked like insects in comparison!
Finally, after what felt like meaningful silence, Vex’thul released a sigh.
The sound carried exhaustion, the kind that came from realizing problems were approaching that strength alone couldn’t solve.
"With how weak you are," he began, his voice rumbling through frequencies that made Noah’s bones resonate, "there’s very little you can do to contribute."
The words hung in the air.
Noah’s current complexity- achievement that had felt monumental moments ago, registered as barely noticeable against the likely hundreds of trillions these beings carried in their everyday existence!
"For our tribe," Vex’thul continued, each word deliberate, "contribution is everything. Effort is everything. Those who cannot contribute, who cannot exert effort that benefits the whole..."

He didn’t finish the sentence, but the implication settled over them like a shroud. In a society where power was currency and everyone was wealthy beyond measure, what happened to those who had nothing to offer?
Effort was everything.
Noah’s lips curved into the faintest smile at hearing this fundamental truth spoken so plainly.
The Seed of the First Farmer, growing within his existence, pulsed with recognition.
These were Early Creatures that had independently discovered what the Principle of Perpetual Harvest encoded...that effort, not result, was the true measure of worth!
Vex’thul’s massive head turned slightly, crystalline features suddenly brightening with the particular expression of someone who had just solved an irritating problem. "Ah, you can do that!"
HUUM!
The enthusiasm in his voice created small aurora in the air, his mood shift so sudden that reality had to scramble to adjust.
He led them toward what Noah initially perceived as another building, but as they approached, his perception revealed it to be something far more complex.
A transparent dome of light rose before them, its surface rippling with distortions. Space and time twisted around it like fabric being wrung by invisible hands.
Inside, impossibility had been made practical, light-years worth of space had been compressed into an area that appeared no larger than a city block from the outside.
And filling this compressed space, mountains and valleys and entire geographical features of it...was manure.
The sheer scale defied comprehension.
Mountain ranges of dung rose toward skies that existed inside a bubble. Valleys carved by rivers of liquid waste wound between hills of compressed feces that had fossilized!
The stench was mercifully contained by the dome, but even seeing it made Noah’s enhanced senses attempt to shut down in self-defense.
"These," Vex’thul announced with the pride of someone showing off treasured resources, "are the excrements of the Cow of Fertility."

chapters.title: Chapter 4112: A Chef! I
paragraphs: He gestured toward the mountains of waste with enthusiasm that suggested he was displaying gold rather than dung.
"Extremely helpful in growing and nurturing herbs. The compression process concentrates the life-giving properties while eliminating the less useful aspects."
He began listing names with the casual expectation that they would mean something. "You can sort it into small compartments and bring it to Creatures Nezan, Digoxin, Yewa..."
Each name was spoken with familiarity that suggested long association, relationships that had persisted through epochs Noah couldn’t imagine.
But...
Sorting shit?!
Noah’s eyes flickered with an expression that went beyond disbelief into something approaching existential insult!
His second journey to the Earliest Folds, his accumulation of power that defied reason, his survival of beings that shouldn’t exist...all to become a dung organizer?
He understood it. This dung was likely extremely unique as he would definitely want it for himself.
But before that...
His gaze swept the surroundings, seeking alternatives.
The village stretched in all directions, surely offering other opportunities for someone of his unique capabilities.
To the far right, past structures that defied architectural possibility, his eyes caught something that made him pause.
A massive table...though calling it a table was like calling an ocean a puddle. The surface alone could have hosted cities, carved from wood that had grown before growth was properly defined.
Upon this table lay a corpse!

It was a Dodo, but to call it simply that was to insult the magnificent impossibility of its existence. Even headless, its neck terminating in a clean cut that suggested violence of incomprehensible scale...the creature radiated power that made Noah’s recent achievements feel like a child’s first steps!
The complexity emanating from the dead flesh exceeded Duke Gwendolyn’s careful accumulation.

The table stood before a cave structure that had been carved into- or perhaps through, a hill that might have been a sleeping titan. The entrance yawned wide enough to swallow buildings, darkness within suggesting depths that connected to spaces that shouldn’t adjoin.

Standing at the table was an Early Creature whose very presence redefined what butchery meant. The Early Creature wielded a blade that lesser civilizations would have worshipped as a weapon of endings. The weapon was the size of a building, yet in his granite hands, it moved with the precision of a scalpel.
He worked with methodical efficiency that suggested infinite practice. Each cut separated meat from bone with understanding that transcended anatomy!
Other Early Creatures gathered around, catching chunks of meat he threw.
They consumed the raw flesh while maintaining conversations.

The casualness of it all...beings who could unmake existence itself treating raw Dodo meat like afternoon snacks- meat from a Duke level entitily...created a surreal domesticity that would make one struggle to compare it to the current age!
"What about that over there?" Noah asked.
Vex’thul’s crystalline eyebrows rose with skepticism that reshaped local probability.

"What about it?" The question carried genuine confusion, as if Noah had asked why water was wet or why existence existed. "The job of Butcher is one that Creature Garvin excels at. You wouldn’t be able to do it better."
He paused, his massive eyes- each one containing depths that suggested infinite crystal recursion, focusing on Noah’s comparatively insignificant form.
"With your power, you cannot even cut the animals, can you?"
The doubt in his voice wasn’t mockery but a genuine question. The complexity differential between Noah and even the dead Dodo was like asking an ant to carve a mountain using wishes!
Under that doubtful gaze, Noah’s eyes pulsed.
"We won’t just be able to butcher," he stated with certainty, "but we’ll do something with our weak hands that will make the experience that much more enjoyable."
Vex’thul’s expression cycled through skepticism, amusement, and finally settled on indulgent curiosity.
He shook his massive head, creating small atmospheric disturbances, but his smile suggested he was willing to humor this impossible claim.
They walked toward the butchering station, their approach drawing attention from the gathered Early Creatures.
As they neared, Vex’thul performed what was clearly a formal greeting- his massive hand rose to his chest and tapped three times in a pattern that created resonance through dimensions.

The gesture left a brief signature in the air, a mark of his existence that would linger for moments before reality reabsorbed it. It was greeting, identification, and respect all encoded in simple motion.
"Garvin," Vex’thul called, his voice carrying across space with the authority of someone who belonged here, "these two Weak Little Things want to prove themselves. Can you give them a chance here?"
Creature Garvin paused in his butchering, his form turning with the deliberate motion of a mountain deciding to notice something.
Up close, Noah could see that his body wasn’t just granite-like...it was granite that had achieved consciousness and decided to try being alive.
His eyebrow rose with skepticism that created local gravitational anomalies. Then he laughed.
The sound redefined what laughter could be.
The laughter created visible ripples in space, each wave carrying amusement!
With a motion that created earthquakes, he sank his massive butcher knife into the table. The blade penetrated the impossibly hard wood with ease.
"Let them be my guests," he boomed, his voice carrying undertones that made stone resonate, "if they can even lift the blade! Bahaha!"
The other Early Creatures joined his laughter, their combined mirth creating a symphony that would have driven lesser beings mad.
They continued eating raw meat with the casualness of beings for whom cooking was unnecessary!
Raw.
The word echoed in Noah’s mind with the particular resonance of opportunity recognized. They were eating it raw, not from necessity but because nothing had suggested they should do otherwise.
His eyes ignited with inspiration that made his companions notice. "Thank you for giving us a chance," he said.
"We, Creatures Osmont and Ozymandias, wish to show you something unique."
The formal introduction using their assumed titles created a ripple of amusement through the gathered beings.

They smiled with indulgence that parents might show children attempting something adorably impossible, continuing their conversations while occasionally glancing over to see what these "Weak Little Things" might attempt.
Their casual strength created an atmosphere of suppressed violence.
Not intentional threat but simply the reality that beings of such power existing in proximity to lesser creatures created danger through presence alone.

A playful gesture from any of them, a friendly pat that exceeded careful control, would obliterate the strongest Dukes Noah had encountered without the Early Creature even noticing they had killed something!
It was fucking overwhelming!
These...were Early Creatures!

Noah and Ozymandias positioned themselves at the head of the butchering table, the massive Dodo corpse stretching before them like a mountain range of meat. This close, Noah could feel the complexity radiating from the dead flesh...power accumulated over epochs that made his own advancement seem like a single day’s growth.
Prompts materialized before his vision with urgency.
|Tremendous Opportunity Detected|
|Material: Lesser Primordial Dodo (Deceased)|
|Warning: Subject exceeds safe interaction parameters by a large factor|
|Attempting to process may result in existential backlash|
|Potential harvest if successful: Glorious waves of loot!|

"Extremely helpful in growing and nurturing herbs.
The compression process concentrates the life-giving properties while eliminating the less useful aspects."
He began listing names with the casual expectation that they would mean something.
"You can sort it into small compartments and bring it to Creatures Nezan, Digoxin, Yewa..."
Each name was spoken with familiarity that suggested long association, relationships that had persisted through epochs Noah couldn’t imagine.
But...
Sorting shit?!
Noah’s eyes flickered with an expression that went beyond disbelief into something approaching existential insult!
His second journey to the Earliest Folds, his accumulation of power that defied reason, his survival of beings that shouldn’t exist...all to become a dung organizer?
He understood it.
This dung was likely extremely unique as he would definitely want it for himself.
But before that...
His gaze swept the surroundings, seeking alternatives.
The village stretched in all directions, surely offering other opportunities for someone of his unique capabilities.
To the far right, past structures that defied architectural possibility, his eyes caught something that made him pause.
A massive table...though calling it a table was like calling an ocean a puddle.
The surface alone could have hosted cities, carved from wood that had grown before growth was properly defined.
Upon this table lay a corpse!
It was a Dodo, but to call it simply that was to insult the magnificent impossibility of its existence.

Even headless, its neck terminating in a clean cut that suggested violence of incomprehensible scale...the creature radiated power that made Noah’s recent achievements feel like a child’s first steps!
The complexity emanating from the dead flesh exceeded Duke Gwendolyn’s careful accumulation.
The table stood before a cave structure that had been carved into- or perhaps through, a hill that might have been a sleeping titan.
The entrance yawned wide enough to swallow buildings, darkness within suggesting depths that connected to spaces that shouldn’t adjoin.
Standing at the table was an Early Creature whose very presence redefined what butchery meant.
The Early Creature wielded a blade that lesser civilizations would have worshipped as a weapon of endings.
The weapon was the size of a building, yet in his granite hands, it moved with the precision of a scalpel.
He worked with methodical efficiency that suggested infinite practice.
Each cut separated meat from bone with understanding that transcended anatomy!
Other Early Creatures gathered around, catching chunks of meat he threw.
They consumed the raw flesh while maintaining conversations.

chapters.title: Chapter 4113: A Chef! II
paragraphs: Noah read the prompts with shining eyes as he prepared to continue regardless.
He closed his eyes, reaching deep into his Early Atlas of the Folds, feeling the constellation of his Towers of Osmont blazing within.
Among them, one tower pulsed with particular warmth...the Cooking Tower of Osmont, containing the True Source of Cooking at Stage Two!
"Begin!" he commanded, the word carrying authority that made even the Early Creatures pause their conversations momentarily.

Ozymandias responded instantly, his tentacle-form arm transforming into an obsidian blade that seemed to drink light. The transformation was perfect...a cutting edge that existed more as concept than physical object, sharpness given form through pure hunger.
The blade descended toward the Dodo’s wing with inevitable certainty.

The first contact revealed the true impossibility of what they were attempting. The skin resisted with the particular stubbornness of matter that had been drenched in trillions of complexity and purity!
|Attempting to cut entity with 52+ Trillion Complexity|
|Success probability: 0.1%|
|Recommendation: Maybe abandon attempt|
Abandon? That was not a word in his quintessential mind!
HUUM!
The blade of Ozymandias’s hand suddenly underwent a transformation that made the watching Early Creatures lean forward slightly.

Millions of microscopic jaws materialized along the cutting edge- not physical mouths but expressions of hunger so pure it had developed dentition. Each jaw expressed the same insatiable need, the same inevitable consumption that defined Ozymandias’s existence.

They devoured the very concept of resistance along the intended path. The blade became not weapon but argument, insisting that separation should occur, and reality, faced with such hungry certainty, reluctantly agreed!
The sensation that flooded through their shared connection was overwhelming.
Noah experienced hunger that transcended sensation!
It was intoxicating and terrifying, feeling his other self literally eat through impossibility.

With effort that made both bodies tremble, Ozymandias’s blade completed its path. The cut was perfect- a single motion that had separated skin that could withstand supernovas, meat that had accumulated power for eons, and bones harder than crystallized time.
|MONUMENTAL ACHIEVEMENT: Successfully Cut 52+ Trillion Complexity Entity|
|Method: Devouring conceptual resistance. Is your Inevitability self actually your strongest weapon?|
|Purity gained by Ozymandias: +250,000,000,000|
|Effort recognized by Perpetual Harvest|
|Bonus for impossible achievement: +50,000,000,000|

The severed wing portion fell to the table with weight that created ripples through dimensions. It was perfectly separated, the cut so clean that it looked artificial- as if reality had simply agreed to be divided rather than being forced.
Noah’s primary body erupted with power that made the Early Creatures’ casual attention sharpen into genuine interest.
Crimson-gold flames burst from his form, but these weren’t mere fire- this was the Authority of Cooking made manifest, pulled from the Tower of Osmont and given free reign.
He channeled everything into this moment!
Every point of complexity and purity he had accumulated, every understanding he had gained, every impossibility he had survived...all of it flowed into the flames that now engulfed the severed wing.
|Attempting to Cook: Primordial Dodo Wing|
|Target Complexity: 52,847,293,018,447|
|Your Complexity: Needs not be mentioned|
|Standard failure rate: 89.999%|
|Analyzing mitigating factors...|
|Resistance of Perpetual Harvest: ACTIVE - Effort multiplied|
|Seed of Principle: Responding. Authority reinforced|
|Atlas of the Folds: Supporting - All Towers contributing|
|Early Creature Heart: Resonating - Fundamental authority engaged|
|Goad: EDUCATING - Reality being taught to allow this|
|Entire existence committed to this single task. How glorious!|
HUUM!
|Recalculated success rate: 95.3%|
|Warning: Failure may result in explosive decompression of complexity|
|Proceed anyway? Of course you will.|
Noah’s existence pulsed as he continued!

The flames engulfed the wing portion, and immediately, something unprecedented began occurring. The Early Creatures, who had been maintaining casual observation, suddenly focused completely. Their conversations ceased. Their consumption of raw meat paused.
They sensed what Noah was wielding to be a Principle as they showed some surprise to yhis. A tiny fraction of it, barely a whisper of what Principles could be, but unmistakably genuine.
The weak thing had actually already grasped something like that?
Noah focused on the task ahead and not on any gazes.
The cooking process transcended simple heating. The flames convinced the meat that it wanted to be cooked, that achieving perfect doneness was its destiny!
Proteins that had existed since before amino acids had names began reorganizing themselves into perfect structural chains.

Each molecule aligned with its neighbors in patterns that maximized both nutritional value and taste. Fats that contained the memory of the Dodo’s million-year life rendered down into liquid gold that would carry flavor beyond what tongues were designed to process!
Ah!
Each portion of the surface of the meat achieved exactly the right degree of caramelization, creating a crust that was simultaneously crispy and yielding, structural and delicate.
The process took seconds that felt like hours, Noah’s perception stretched to experience every moment of transformation!
He felt the meat’s resistance give way to acceptance, then enthusiasm. It wanted to be perfect. Under the influence of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest, even being cooked became a form of growth.
Then, with a flash that made several Early Creatures expectant, it was complete.
The wing lay transformed on the table, and the aroma that rose from it made even these ancient beings salivate.
This wasn’t merely the smell of cooked meat...this was the scent of comfort, of satisfaction before beings knew they could be satisfied, of home before the concept of home existed!

The exterior had achieved a perfect bronze-gold crust that seemed to glow with its own light. The caramelization was so precise that each scale of former skin had become a tiny mirror, reflecting not light but the very concept of flavor.
Wisps of steam rose from it carrying aromatic compounds that shouldn’t exist- molecules that triggered memories of meals that hadn’t happened yet!
If one were to cut through that perfect crust, the interior would reveal a masterpiece of temperature gradients.

The outer layer had been seared to seal in every drop of primordial juice, transitioning through perfect pink that deepened toward a center maintaining just enough red to preserve the Dodo’s essential nature!
The fat had rendered into pockets of liquid gold that would burst on contact with taste, releasing flavors that contained entire histories of evolution.
|IMPOSSIBLE ACHIEVEMENT COMPLETED|
|Successfully Cooked: Primordial Dodo Wing|
|Quality: Legendary (Perfect Medium-Rare)|
|Temperature achieved: 30 Million degrees celsius at center, 75 million at the crust|
|Complexity of meal: profound|
|Note: Cooking process has amplified base complexity by 42%|
|Due to monumental effort in cooking:|
|Cooking Tower of Osmont progressing to Stage Three|
|Complexity gained: +200,000,000,000|
|New Title Acquired: Chef of the Verdant Eternia Tribe|
The Prompts came one after another as Noah felt his Atlas buzzing, a tower roaring out and proceeding ahead as it became an even grander light house that would illuminate the way forward!
|Item Created: Perfectly Cooked Primordial Dodo Wing|
|Prepared by: Noah Osmont, Early Creature Chef|
|Cooking method: Principle-Enhanced Searing|
|Doneness: Medium-Rare (optimal for complexity absorption)|
|Effect if consumed: +500,000,000,000 Complexity|
|Effect if consumed: +500,000,000,000 Purity|
|Additional effect: Understanding of Primordial Tastes|
|Additional effect: Temporary perception of flavor dimensions|
|Warning: Consumption may cause existential pleasure|
"Outsider," Khor’s voice resonated through his consciousness with genuine amazement, "you continue to surprise me."

Noah surprised himself as he stared at the perfectly cooked wing. His mouth actually watered...something that shouldn’t happen to beings of his level. The biological response transcended his transcendent nature.

Before he could move, before he could even consider tasting his own creation, a massive granite hand moved with speed that defied its size. Creature Garvin snatched the wing with the particular greed of someone who had just discovered something they didn’t know they needed.
He raised the wing to his mouth- jaws that could have swallowed cities opening with anticipation.
The Early Creature didn’t nibble or taste- he consumed the entire wing in a single motion, teeth that could crush concepts making short work of the perfectly cooked meat.
The transformation was immediate and profound.

Garvin’s eyes, formations of living granite that had witnessed eons- suddenly pulsed with new light. His expression shifted through a spectrum of emotions that his face hadn’t bothered expressing in millennia: surprise at the initial flavor, delight as the complexity hit, something approaching euphoria as the full impact registered.
The other Early Creatures had stopped everything.
Every eye, organs that perceived across dimensions- focused on Garvin’s expression.
He chewed slowly, deliberately, his massive form actually trembling slightly as flavor compounds that shouldn’t exist triggered responses in beings that thought they had experienced everything!
The golden fat burst across his tongue, releasing tastes that contained the Dodo’s entire evolutionary history compressed into sensation.
The perfectly cooked protein delivered understanding, each bite teaching something about what food could be when elevated beyond mere sustenance.
The silence stretched, reality itself holding its breath to see the verdict.

Garvin swallowed, the motion visible as the food traveled down his massive throat. His eyes, now blazing with inner light that hadn’t been there before, turned to Noah and Ozymandias. The weight of his gaze felt like mountains leaning in to look at pebbles.

Then his attention expanded to include Vex’thul and the other gathered Early Creatures. The combined focus of their interest created pressure that made existence question whether it should continue existing in their presence.
They spoke in perfect unison, voices harmonizing across frequencies that shouldn’t overlap, creating a single word that carried the force of Existence itself.
"More!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4114: A Glorious Symphony!
paragraphs: The Early Creatures sought more, their unified demand still reverberating through local space. But what was truly remarkable was the nature of their observation...these weren’t simple beings demanding food like hungry animals.
Each one possessed over ten thousand Kleos Glyphs, their perception operating on levels that saw everything!
They had witnessed Noah’s entire process with perfect clarity.
The flash of Principle hadn’t escaped them...that tiny fraction of Perpetual Harvest he wielded had been noted, catalogued, understood.
But more interesting to them was the unique authority he had displayed.
"Cooking...?" one of them murmured,"That should originate from Living Conceptual Authority, should it not?"
They could see his methodology completely.
With their terrifying power and accumulated knowledge, they could likely replicate what he had done within moments of trying.

The patterns were clear, the energy flows obvious, the transformation of matter into elevated matter simply a puzzle they had already solved by watching. There were only a few parts they couldn’t imitate that seemed to be unique to him!
But if they truly wanted, they could now do something 80% similar!
Yet they didn’t.
Their faces carried easy smiles, the expressions of ancient beings who had found something novel in existence that had long ago run out of surprises.
This young Early Creature was teaching them something...not the technique, which they had already grasped, but the joy of discovery, the pleasure of being served rather than serving themselves.
They would not steal such methodology quickly. That would make the young Early Creature less special, and they were secure enough in their power to allow others to shine!
It was the confidence of beings who knew they were already brilliant...they could afford to let smaller lights flicker without feeling diminished.
Noah sensed this goodwill radiating from them like warmth from stars. He sighed internally, a complex emotion washing through him.
Some Early Creatures, it seemed, were genuinely good. Not kind by necessity or social contract, but good because they had chosen to be despite having the power to be otherwise.
Since they held goodwill, he would return it amplified.
He nodded toward Ozymandias, and his other self responded instantly.
Both arms transformed into stellar obsidian blades with edges that weren’t sharp but hungry- cutting implements that achieved separation through consumption rather than division.
Ozymandias began the arduous task of properly butchering the remaining Dodo. This was methodical disassembly following principles of butchery!

First, he separated the breast- two massive portions of white meat that would have fed armies. Then the thighs, dense with dark meat that had supported the creature’s impossible weight. The drumsticks followed, then the wings’ remaining portion.

He carved out the tenderloin with particular care- that precious strip of meat that ran along the spine, tender beyond description even in its raw state. The back was sectioned, and finally, the organs were set aside- Noah’s eyes flashing brightly as he did not plan to use them!
Eight parts in total, each one a monument to impossible biology.
|Successfully sectioned 52+ Trillion Complexity Entity|
|Effort recognized: Unprecedented for your level|
|Purity gained by Ozymandias: +1,500,000,000,000|
|NEW DISTINCTION EARNED: Early Butcher|
|Effect: Offensive cutting against entities below 50 Trillion Complexity enhanced 10x|
|Devouring efficiency increased proportionally|
|This distinction will elevate with continued butchering of powerful beings|
|Current level: Initiate|
|Next level requirements: Butcher 100 entities above 10 Trillion Complexity|
Oh!
Glorious sets of prompts arose as they caused one’s eyes to water with majesty!
Noah raised his arms like a conductor before an invisible orchestra, and reality responded to his gesture.
|The Weavings of Tyranny ring gloriously true|
|The Symphony of the Protagonist echoes out in the Verdant Eternia Tribe|
His existence buzzed as the Protagonist Tower of Osmont and Tyranny Tower of Osmont blazed within his Atlas.
Sounds that shouldn’t exist began manifesting...drums that beat with the rhythm of stories yet to be told, trumpets that announced victories not yet achieved.
The music came from nowhere and everywhere, a soundtrack to impossibility about to unfold.

The eight portions of Dodo meat rose into the air at his gesture, each one surrounded by its own nimbus of crimson-gold flame. This wasn’t sequential cooking but simultaneous transformation- eight instances of impossible achievement happening in parallel!
The flames danced to the rhythm of the invisible drums, each beat making them pulse with greater intensity.
The meat began its transformation, proteins reorganizing themselves in time with the music, fats rendering in harmony with melodies.
|Eight simultaneous transformations at 52+ Trillion Complexity|
|Failure probability...Cannot calculate odds this low|
|This is actually insane, but you’re going to do it anyway so let’s see what happens|

Even his Weavings of Existence- the distinction of the Weaver of Existence and the System of Existence flowing through him, his Infiniverse, and Early Veiled Shore which established truths and presented the challenges of existence in the form of prompts...even this system doubted!
And yet he went on.
DUM! DUM! DUM!
The symphony picked up tempo.
The cooking process became performance art.
Noah’s hands moved through the air, conducting temperature and time like musical notes.

Each gesture adjusted the heat on different portions, the breast receiving gentle flames that preserved its delicate nature, the thighs getting intense heat that would break down their denser fibers, the tenderloin barely kissed by fire to maintain its buttery texture.
DUM!

The Symphony grew louder, more complex, as if existence itself had decided to provide accompaniment to this moment of culinary transcendence. Early Creatures who had been approaching from other parts of the village stopped to watch, drawn by music that touched something primal even in beings that predated primality.
His Glyphs contributed As Perpetual Harvest bathed everything.
His Heart.
His Atlas. His Towers. His Everything! All of it contributed and burned fiercly like an engine!
|Cooking Progress: 25%|
|Complexity rising due to immense resonance|
|Cooking Progress: 75%|
|Warning: Deliciousness approaching critical mass. Nearby Early Creatures beginning to drool|
HUUM!
|Cooking Progress: 100%|
|An astounding achievement! Eight Legendary wonders born simultaneously!|
The music reached crescendo as Noah threw his arms wide, a swirling infinity symbol of crimson-gold flames manifesting around him with the Authority of Cooking at its center.
The eight perfectly cooked portions hung in space, each one glowing with its own inner light, steam rising from them!

chapters.title: Chapter 4115: Measure of Growth!
paragraphs: Creature Vex’thul, Creature Garvin, and the others moved forward with shining eyes.
Their massive hands reached for the floating portions with care that suggested they understood they were about to experience something transformative.
They bit into the meat simultaneously, and the collective response was silence...the kind that occurs when experience transcends language’s ability to describe it.
Serenity and glory spread all around!
Noah opened his eyes to witness rows of prompts cascading before his vision.
|Achievement- The Feast of Impossibility!|
|You just cooked for Entities that eat concepts of existence themselves. Such effort is profoundly awarded.|
|Complexity gained: +500,000,000,000|
|Cooking Tower of Osmont: Stage Three achieved!|
|New abilities unlocked: Conceptual Cuisine|
|You can now cook ideas. No, really.|
|Title Evolved: Master Chef of the Verdant Eternia Tribe|
|Respect level among Early Creatures: "That Young One Can COOK"|
|Special Recognition from Perpetual Harvest:|
|This counts as effort in ways that is still calculating|
|2% Principle Authority stabilizing...|
|Actually, make that 2.1%|
|The Principle itself is entertained|
|Final Statistics for this Cooking Session:|
|Total Complexity gained: 750,000,000,000|
|Total Purity gained: 750,000,000,000|
|Early Creatures impressed: All those observing nearby|
|Manure sorted: Still zero|
|Career path: Definitively established|
|Additional Note: Remember when you were worried about sorting shit?|
The Early Creatures continued eating with expressions of rapture that would have been comical on beings of such power if it weren’t so genuine.
They had tasted something new... the idea that food could be more than fuel, more than sustenance.
It could be art!
And oh, could a certain entity be artistic!
Noah and Ozymandias settled onto the ground near the butchering table, their forms finally able to relax after the intense performance of cooking for beings that could unmake reality with thoughts.
The nearby Early Creatures continued their feast with expressions of contentment that made the air itself taste sweeter.
Noah could feel the complexity coursing through him like liquid starlight in his veins.
Each heartbeat distributed the power further, integrating it into his fundamental existence. He pulled up his status to gauge exactly how far he had come.
|NOAH OSMONT, The Early Creature. Age 1/90. 236,555 Drops of Blood|
|Total Complexity: 4,237,293,847,291(4 Trillion+)|
|Total Purity: 4,237,293,847,291(4 Trillion+)|
|Existence Level: Approaching Duke-Threshold|
|GLYPHS POSSESSED:|
|- Kleos Glyph of the Creature’s First Lesson(Forehead)|
|- Seed of Perpetual Harvest Glyphs x3 (Forehead, Palms)|
|Total: 4 Active Glyphs|
|DISTINCTIONS(Too many):|
|- True Emperor of Quintessence|
|- True Emperor of Tyranny|
|- True Emperor of Infinity|
|- The Early Creature|
|- Master Chef of the Verdant Eternia Tribe|
|- Member of Verdant Eternia Tribe...|
|- The Living Existential Guider...|
|TOOLS:|
|- The Goad (Rearing Stick of Existential Education)|
|- Slipper of Existential Humiliation (Left)|
|Resistances...Towers...Heart...(Do you really want the full list?)|
He was proceeding along gloriously as there were still 22 hours left!
Beside him, Ozymandias’s simpler status reflected his pure nature:
|OZYMANDIAS - THE PUREST HUNGER|
|Complexity: 0 (Converted to Purity)|
|DISTINCTIONS:|
|- Inevitability of Recursive Hunger|
|- Early Butcher (Initiate Level)|
|- Member of Verdant Eternia Tribe|
Noah’s attention fixed on one particular achievement within his existence- the Cooking Tower of Osmont had reached Stage Three, and with it came an ability that defied comprehension.
He could now cook concepts. Not metaphorically, not symbolically, but literally take an abstract idea and transform it through culinary process into something that could be consumed.

The implications were heavy. Could he cook the concept of victory and feed it to someone before battle? Take the idea of understanding and serve it as a meal? Cook the idea of Order and feed it to Sigrid? There were many things to think of!
But that contemplation would need to wait.
Noah looked toward the content figures of Creature Vex’thul and Creature Garvin, who were still savoring the lingering taste of their feast.
"Might I keep the slightly less valuable organs?" Noah asked, his tone carefully casual.
The Early Creatures exchanged glances, and smiles spread across their massive faces.

They knew- of course they knew, that the organs were just as valuable if not more than some parts. The heart that had pumped blood through a creature of fifty trillion complexity, the liver that had filtered primordial toxins, the gizzard that had ground down matter that shouldn’t be digestible. These were treasures beyond measure.
Creature Garvin waved his granite hand with casual generosity. "I caught this little bird, so I can give away what remains of it. Consider it payment for the experience you’ve provided."
His voice carried warmth that made stone seem soft. "We’ve eaten the same meals for epochs. Taste had become just another sensation. You reminded us it could be pleasure."
Noah nodded and waved his hand toward the remaining Dodo parts.
The effort to store something of such complexity made his existence strain...these organs radiated power that exceeded entire pantheons of common Dukes!
But into his storage they went, treasures for future use.
The Early Creatures returned to their conversations, but now with new energy, discussing flavors and textures with the enthusiasm of new discovery.
Their joy was genuine, uncomplicated by the politics and power plays that Noah had expected.

Khor’s voice resonated in his mind with contemplative weight. "Early Creatures were unique beings, Outsider. Stemming from the Everythings of THE Creature itself, they were meant to embody the best of what existence could become. Many did exactly that...became paragons of power used wisely."
She paused, her consciousness fragment pulsing with ancient memory.

"Very few can say exactly what happened for some Early Creatures to eventually act the way they did...the cruelty, the destruction, the mad hunger for more than existence could provide. Some say the Early Veiled Shores made by THE Creature and THE Living Existences were the catalyst, creating isolation that bred paranoia. Others blame THE Living Paradox...and who knows, maybe thay schemer did do something. Others blame the accumulation of power itself, that too much complexity without wisdom becomes its own form of madness."
Noah reflected on her words analytically.
The Early Creatures here showed none of the madness or cruelty he had been warned about and observed personally!
So truly...what had happened?!

chapters.title: Chapter 4116: The Arrival of Unity! I
paragraphs: They were powerful beyond measure but used that power with restraint that suggested wisdom earned through experience.
"Were you moved to speechlessness?"
Vex’thul’s voice came from behind him, the massive creature having approached with silence that defied his size. His crystalline face carried a knowing smile.

"This is how the Verdant Eternia Tribe is," he continued, his tone becoming serious despite the smile remaining. "We help each other. Existence is vast and immeasurable...we’re all trying to understand it and how to better exist within it."
He settled his massive form nearby, the ground accepting his weight with the resignation of matter that knew it had no choice.

"Many things require effort and can involve great danger. Hunting the creatures we eat, defending against those like Gilgamesh who would change what we’ve built, even simple survival in the First Folds where everything can kill everything else."
His eyes...crystals containing crystals in infinite recursion focused on Noah with warmth.

"But elevating and helping other Early Creatures? That’s an act that costs us nothing yet could mean everything to them. You’re weak by our standards- this is simple fact. We could have sent you to sort waste, had you perform menial tasks that matched your power level. Instead, we gave you a chance to show us something new."
He gestured toward the other Early Creatures still discussing their meal.

"And you did. The cost to us was nothing- some meat we would have eaten anyway. But you’ve given us experience, novelty, a new way to appreciate something we had taken for granted. That’s how civilization should work...not zero-sum competition where one must lose for another to win, but mutual elevation where everyone rises together."
The philosophy was simple yet profound, especially coming from beings who could have easily chosen might over right!
They had power to take everything, yet chose to give. Strength to dominate, yet decided to collaborate.

Noah felt something shift in his understanding of what the First Folds represented. Not just an era of raw power and primitive existence, but perhaps the first attempt at something greater...beings learning that existence could be more than survival, that power could be used for more than dominance.
The question that lingered was what had changed between then and now. What had transformed some of these philosophical, helpful creatures into the nightmares that haunted the stories of his era?

Perhaps, Noah thought as he watched the Early Creatures continue their animated discussions about food they had just discovered could taste good, perhaps the answer lay not in what they became but in what existence did to them over the eons that followed.
Time had a way of wearing down even the strongest principles, and countless epochs and eons was a very long time to maintain goodness in the face of existence’s tendency toward entropy.

But for now, in this moment, in this village that shouldn’t exist populated by beings that defied comprehension, there was genuine community. And Noah had found his place in it not through power but through providing something no one knew they needed!

Creature Vex’thul looked toward Noah with renewed interest, his crystalline features reflecting anticipation. "Os, Ozy, do your little existences still have the capability to continue? We can go out to hunt some genuinely good game here for an even larger feast-"
HUUUM!
The words died unfinished as Vex’thul’s eyes suddenly blazed with alarm.
His massive head snapped upward, and around them, every Early Creature in the vicinity mirrored the motion with expressions that had shifted from contentment to concern.
Up.
They all looked up.
Because there, in the skies above the vast Verdant Eternia Tribe that extended for light-years in every direction, dozens of massive forms had materialized.

Early Creatures of various configurations...some humanoid with perfect proportions that made beauty seem inadequate, others bestial with features that predated the separation of predator and prey, still others that were pure concepts given form or elements that had achieved consciousness.
But they all shared something that made the Verdant Eternia natives tense- they didn’t bear the verdant teardrop marking of the tribe.
Noah’s eyes flashed cold with immediate understanding. Just when his journey had been proceeding with unexpected smoothness, reality had remembered it was supposed to be dangerous.
He complained internally about the timing while knowing this was exactly why the First Folds carried a 99% mortality rate.
|The Weavings of the Protagonist comfort you with honesty:|
|This is the core of your existence- conflict and growth|
|Tremendous gifts obtained in sequence was suspicious|
|Frankly, we’re surprised the peace lasted this long|
|The trumpets of adventure and trials now ring as Failure or death: Highly probable|
|Rebirth and transformation: Possible if you survive|
|Recommended strategy: Retreat remains viable option|
His weavings buzzed as his Atlas shone brightly!
Noah observed the newly arrived Early Creatures with eyes that catalogued every detail.

Waves of power radiated from them that made the air itself genuflect. On their foreheads blazed a marking distinctly different from the verdant teardrop- a symbol that seemed to be fire given geometric form, angular lines that suggested both power and war, conquest made into signature.

More disturbing was how the marking appeared superimposed, as if it had been placed over something else. The edges showed signs of covering previous tribal marks, like a flag planted over conquered territory.
Their clothing marked them as something beyond typical Early Creatures.

While the Verdant Eternia tribe wore practical garments or went without, these beings were adorned in what could only be called simple regalia. Furs that gleamed with inner light, jewelry carved from concepts themselves!
But most distinctive was the garment they all shared...chitons of stellar gold that draped their forms with classical elegance.
Chitons!
The garments fell from one shoulder, leaving the other bare, secured at the waist with belts that looked forged from compressed starlight.
The fabric itself seemed alive, moving with winds that existed in other dimensions, each fold catching light that hadn’t been invented yet.
These weren’t random raiders or wandering Early Creatures. This was an army in uniform, beings who had surrendered individual identity for collective purpose.

From among them, one figure descended with the particular grace of someone who knew others would make way. Larger than his companions, his fair skin gleamed like polished boulder, each muscle carved with precision that suggested existence itself had been his sculptor.
His jaw could have been used to demonstrate the concept of determination, his entire form radiating strength that seemed hundreds of times grander than any Dukes in Noahs current era!

The cost to us was nothing- some meat we would have eaten anyway.
But you’ve given us experience, novelty, a new way to appreciate something we had taken for granted.
That’s how civilization should work...not zero-sum competition where one must lose for another to win, but mutual elevation where everyone rises together."
The philosophy was simple yet profound, especially coming from beings who could have easily chosen might over right!
They had power to take everything, yet chose to give.
Strength to dominate, yet decided to collaborate.
Noah felt something shift in his understanding of what the First Folds represented.

Not just an era of raw power and primitive existence, but perhaps the first attempt at something greater...beings learning that existence could be more than survival, that power could be used for more than dominance.
The question that lingered was what had changed between then and now.
What had transformed some of these philosophical, helpful creatures into the nightmares that haunted the stories of his era?

Perhaps, Noah thought as he watched the Early Creatures continue their animated discussions about food they had just discovered could taste good, perhaps the answer lay not in what they became but in what existence did to them over the eons that followed.
Time had a way of wearing down even the strongest principles, and countless epochs and eons was a very long time to maintain goodness in the face of existence’s tendency toward entropy.
But for now, in this moment, in this village that shouldn’t exist populated by beings that defied comprehension, there was genuine community.
And Noah had found his place in it not through power but through providing something no one knew they needed!
Creature Vex’thul looked toward Noah with renewed interest, his crystalline features reflecting anticipation.
"Os, Ozy, do your little existences still have the capability to continue?
We can go out to hunt some genuinely good game here for an even larger feast-"
HUUUM!
The words died unfinished as Vex’thul’s eyes suddenly blazed with alarm.
His massive head snapped upward, and around them, every Early Creature in the vicinity mirrored the motion with expressions that had shifted from contentment to concern.
Up.
They all looked up.
Because there, in the skies above the vast Verdant Eternia Tribe that extended for light-years in every direction, dozens of massive forms had materialized.

Early Creatures of various configurations...some humanoid with perfect proportions that made beauty seem inadequate, others bestial with features that predated the separation of predator and prey, still others that were pure concepts given form or elements that had achieved consciousness.
But they all shared something that made the Verdant Eternia natives tense- they didn’t bear the verdant teardrop marking of the tribe.
Noah’s eyes flashed cold with immediate understanding.
Just when his journey had been proceeding with unexpected smoothness, reality had remembered it was supposed to be dangerous.
He complained internally about the timing while knowing this was exactly why the First Folds carried a 99% mortality rate.
|The Weavings of the Protagonist comfort you with honesty:|
|This is the core of your existence- conflict and growth|
|Tremendous gifts obtained in sequence was suspicious|
|Frankly, we’re surprised the peace lasted this long|
|The trumpets of adventure and trials now ring as Failure or death: Highly probable|
|Rebirth and transformation: Possible if you survive|
|Recommended strategy: Retreat remains viable option|
His weavings buzzed as his Atlas shone brightly!
Noah observed the newly arrived Early Creatures with eyes that catalogued every detail.
Waves of power radiated from them that made the air itself genuflect.

On their foreheads blazed a marking distinctly different from the verdant teardrop- a symbol that seemed to be fire given geometric form, angular lines that suggested both power and war, conquest made into signature.
More disturbing was how the marking appeared superimposed, as if it had been placed over something else.
The edges showed signs of covering previous tribal marks, like a flag planted over conquered territory.
Their clothing marked them as something beyond typical Early Creatures.
While the Verdant Eternia tribe wore practical garments or went without, these beings were adorned in what could only be called simple regalia.
Furs that gleamed with inner light, jewelry carved from concepts themselves!
But most distinctive was the garment they all shared...chitons of stellar gold that draped their forms with classical elegance.
Chitons!
The garments fell from one shoulder, leaving the other bare, secured at the waist with belts that looked forged from compressed starlight.
The fabric itself seemed alive, moving with winds that existed in other dimensions, each fold catching light that hadn’t been invented yet.
These weren’t random raiders or wandering Early Creatures.
This was an army in uniform, beings who had surrendered individual identity for collective purpose.
From among them, one figure descended with the particular grace of someone who knew others would make way.
Larger than his companions, his fair skin gleamed like polished boulder, each muscle carved with precision that suggested existence itself had been his sculptor.
His jaw could have been used to demonstrate the concept of determination, his entire form radiating strength that seemed hundreds of times grander than any Dukes in Noahs current era!

chapters.title: Chapter 4117: The Arrival of Unity! II
paragraphs: Dark hair wild as primordial storms framed features that would inspire art across eons.
When he spoke, his voice carried with the cadence of absolute certainty- each word placed with precision, building to conclusions that seemed inevitable once stated.
"In Existence," he began, his voice reaching every ear despite not shouting, "do you know what is most important?"
He paused, letting the question settle into consciousness before continuing.

"Some say power- the ability to impose will upon reality. Others claim knowledge, understanding the mechanisms behind what is. Still others insist on freedom, the right to exist without interference."
His gaze swept across the hundreds of dispersed Early Creatures of the Verdant Eternia Tribe, each one feeling personally addressed.
"But truly, something else is more important. Unity."
The word rang with the force of revelation, as if he had just discovered and was sharing fundamental truth.

"Unity is not uniformity...we need not all be the same. Unity is not submission, we need not all bow to one will. Unity is understanding that we are stronger together than apart, that our individual greatnesses can combine into something transcendent."
He descended further, now floating at a height where his presence loomed without requiring him to look down.

"Consider: we Early Creatures possess power that reshapes Existence with thought. Yet we scatter across the First Folds in tiny tribes, each hoarding our small wisdoms, our petty treasures. Meanwhile, existence itself grows more complex, more dangerous. New threats emerge while we remain divided."
His voice grew more intense, more certain.

"From among us, The First Leader has risen to achieve Unity for all Early Creatures. Not unity through conquest, though he could conquer. Not unity through fear, though he is fearsome. Unity through vision....showing us what we could become if we stood together."
He spread his arms wide, the golden chiton catching light that made him seem to glow from within.

"I am Lysander the Voice, and I stand here today as a Representative of The First Leader, Gilgamesh, to ask the Verdant Eternia Tribe to join him in Unity. To become part of the Gilgamesh Sovereignty where all Early Creatures will stand as one, sharing knowledge, sharing power, sharing the burden of shepherding existence toward what it should become."
The name hung in the air with weight- the Gilgamesh Sovereignty!
Not a tribe but something larger, an entity that transcended traditional structures.
"All those here are invited to join. Your uniqueness will be preserved, your traditions respected. You would simply add your strength to ours, and receive our strength in return. Unity."
His expression shifted slightly, sincere regret mixing with implacable determination.
"But I understand that sometimes, a bit of force is required for true Unity. Old patterns resist change. Comfort resists growth. So I wonder..."
He paused, letting tension build with the skill of an orator who had given this speech across multiple tribes.
"Today, will Unity be peaceful? Or will it require some force?"
HUUM!

The question wasn’t really a question. The dozens of Early Creatures floating behind him, all wearing the same golden chitons, all bearing the same superimposed mark of the Sovereignty, made clear that force was not just available but expected.
The Verdant Eternia Tribe had just been given an offer that wasn’t really an offer, a choice that wasn’t really a choice.
Join or be joined.
Unite or be united.
The feast that had brought such joy moments ago suddenly seemed like a last meal before everything changed.
Unity through peace, or unity through force?
The words echoed across existence with weight that made reality itself pause to consider the implications.
Then, in the next moment, right after the words...Lysander’s body pulsed as he released a golden light that blanketed everything!
A golden light.
And with it...the trembling began!
HUUUM!
But this trembling was nothing like what Noah had experienced when Schrodinger appeared to close the tear in the Temporal Folds.
The two phenomena were so vastly different in scale that comparison became meaningless...like comparing a ripple to a tsunami, a spark to a supernova!
Oh!
Prompts erupted before Noah’s vision with urgency.
|Catastrophic External Pressure detected|
|Source: Haki of Lysander the Voice|
|Your existence has been placed under strain exceeding all parameters|
|TEMPORARY STATUS SUPPRESSION ACTIVE|
|All accumulated power: NULLIFIED|
|EXISTENTIAL LIMITATIONS IMPOSED:|
|Movement: RESTRICTED|
|Speech: RESTRICTED|
|Authority usage: BLOCKED|
|CRITICAL WARNING:|
|Capability to move is no longer available|
|All surrounding existence is under the control of Lysander’s Haki|
|Current options: Live or Die|
|Your input on this matter: Not requested|
Noah read these prompts as his body stood frozen, not even his eyes able to move from where they had been looking when the pressure descended.
His existence didn’t become fearful...he had given away his fear. It didn’t doubt, his doubt had been sacrificed.
But what he felt was Tyranny. What he felt at this moment was...pure, undiluted waves of Tyranny!

All that he was, every point of complexity and purity he had fought to accumulate, every impossible achievement, every transcendent moment...nullified by the mere aura of an Early Creature who wasn’t even trying to suppress him specifically.
He was just collateral pressure from a being making a point.
The helplessness was absolute, and it was the one thing he used to fear before he had given fear away.
This specific helplessness that one day, in his Infiniverse or his homeworld, an unknown being would appear whose sheer existence would make resistance impossible.
That all his preparation, all his growth, all his careful planning would mean nothing before overwhelming force that didn’t even notice him as it passed.
He had given away the fear of this, but now he was living in such a situation.
An enemy he hadn’t expected, didn’t know existed until moments ago, and without even making a conscious move against him, had placed his life entirely in their hands!
He hated this.
He hated it with intensity that made his frozen existence burn internally!
And at such a pivotal moment...a voice echoed out.

"In what remains of my memory," Khor’s voice echoed in his mind, carrying weight of personal experience, "I remember feeling helpless against THE Living Paradox. After it had weakened me, I couldn’t lift a finger. Couldn’t summon the hunger that defined me. Couldn’t even properly exist in rebellion."
Her consciousness fragment pulsed with remembered pain.
"THE Living Paradox mocked me as I lay there. ’Is this truly The First Hunger?’ it said with such disappointment. ’Seems like nothing more than any common Inevitability. What a waste of reputation.’"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4118: Helplessness!
paragraphs: She paused, the memory clearly still affecting her despite the eons passed.
"I took it calmly. What else could I do? I asked why- why hunt someone like me? What could THE Living Paradox hope to achieve by erasing something that had existed since existence learned to want?"
Her voice carried bitter amusement.

"It replied with mockery that cut deeper than the cessation it was imposing. ’A creature like you would never understand. What I’m doing is actually mercy- you won’t have to be there for the Fallout.’ As if my erasure was kindness, protecting me from something worse."
WAA!
Noah’s weavings buzzed as he heard this!
What could someone as astonishing as Khor not understand?
And what was meant by...Fallout?!
The weight of ancient exhaustion colored her words.

"At that moment, I just felt so tired. Tired of consuming without satisfaction. Tired of being feared. Tired of existing as appetite without fulfillment. I could have struggled- my nature alone should have made me fight. I could have called upon countless Inevitabilities that owed me their existence. I could have Hungered. I could have made THE Living Paradox work for my cessation."
She sighed, the sound containing regrets that transcended time.
"But I was tired. So I did nothing. I simply sighed and accepted what was coming. After that, all that came was nothing- not even the memory of having been."
Her consciousness fragment pulsed with intensity that hadn’t been there before.

"When I think about that choice now, with this second chance at existence, I regret it profoundly. I wish I hadn’t just done nothing. I wish I had done something. Anything. I wish... I had done Everything."
BOOM!
Her voice suddenly blazed with fierce determination.

"In the face of utter helplessness, will you do nothing, Outsider? Because even in utter helplessness, you still have Everything. Every Everything you haven’t given away, every aspect of your existence that remains. You could fight with Everything you have, even if fighting seems impossible. Even if it is impossible. If you still die...hey, at least you gave it your everything."
BOOM!
The words resonated through Noah’s frozen form with force- heavy force.
He didn’t necessarily need the encouragement- he would always fight regardless of odds. But her words were consoling nonetheless, a reminder that even the impossible had been attempted before.
Even though he couldn’t move his lips or body, he roared within his existence.
He roared against the helplessness that sought to define him.
He roared with Tyranny that refused to acknowledge any authority but its own.
He roared with Quintessence that insisted on the fundamental rightness of his continued existence.
He roared with Infinity that suggested limits were merely suggestions he hadn’t gotten around to ignoring yet.
His entire existence lit up internally like a star being born in slow motion. Every Tower of Osmont blazed with defiance!
His Atlas burned with maps to pasts and futures where he wasn’t suppressed. His heart beat with rhythm that insisted movement was his right, not Lysander’s to grant or deny.

He sought to defy something that couldn’t be defied- the aura, the Haki of something with countless quadrillions of complexity. The mathematical impossibility of it didn’t matter. Mathematics had been wrong about him before.
The Principle of Perpetual Harvest stirred within him, recognizing effort beyond effort, the attempt to move when movement had been forbidden by existence itself.
This was what it meant to be without fear or doubt. Not the absence of danger or uncertainty, but the refusal to let either stop you from trying!
Oh!
Even frozen, even suppressed to complexity of 1, even with his very existence hanging on the whim of a being who could unmake him with a thought- Noah fought!
Because that’s what he did.
That’s who he was.
The Early Creature... who would now attempt impossible resistance.
Noah’s defiance caused his internal existence to buzz with rebellion!
With glorious, quintessential defiance!
Then, an instant later, something that had been dormant stirred to life.
|The slumbering weavings of Cheats have been awoken|
|An unprecedented situation has triggered this slumbering authority|
HUUM!
Cheats.
The glorious paradoxical conceptual Source that also defined him, that had been quiet for a while and only rose when it needed to!
Now it rose amidst his raging Tyranny of defiance, awakened by impossibility that demanded impossible solutions.
|Tremendous effort beyond all efforts detected|
|Attempting to bypass immovable force|
|All authority has been nullified by external pressure|
|And yet...|
|The Authority of Cheats burns luminously|
|Because this IS its nature|
|To function when function is forbidden|
BOOM!
Deep within Noah’s existence, a pair of terrifying golden eyes opened.
They gazed upon everything with unfathomable regality and arrogance that suggested rules were merely suggestions they found amusing.
These weren’t physical eyes but the conceptual gaze of Cheats itself- the embodiment of bypassing set norms and limitations, of finding the loophole in reality’s programming.
The golden eyes moved across his suppressed existence with the particular interest of someone examining a puzzle they found entertaining!

They rose to his Early Atlas of the Folds, where only a single tower remained lit while all others stood dark and suppressed- the Tower of Cheats itself, refusing to acknowledge that it should be extinguished.
The golden eyes gazed coldly at everything with assessment that transcended normal perception. Then, a prompt materialized that shouldn’t have been possible!
|The Weavings of Cheats arrive before the Quintessential Tower of Osmont|
|Question is posed: Your limits are nullified|
|So why not just step from the limit of the Second Stage into the Third?|
HUUM!
|Rules say you cannot advance under suppression|
|But when have rules mattered to Cheats?|
The Quintessence Tower of Osmont buzzed with sudden possibility!
The logic was absurd- advancing under complete suppression should be impossible. But Cheats didn’t care about should or shouldn’t. It cared about finding the gap between them.
An instant later, sealed light began to shine from within the tower’s structure.
|The Early Sacred Living Quintessence Tower of Osmont has silently stepped into the Third Stage of a Vital Lighthouse|
|Method: Cheating|
|Legitimacy: Who’s asking?|

Under tremendous suppression, at a time when no authority should function, when even breathing was a granted privilege rather than a right, a defiant authority moved its golden gaze from Quintessence toward another tower.
The Early Sacred Living Existence Tower of Osmont.
His concept of Existence itself, the tower he had built to house his understanding of being.
The golden eyes of Cheats gazed at it with the same arrogant certainty, asking the same impossible question: Why not advance? Why accept limitation when limitation could be ignored?

The Existence Tower buzzed under that gaze, not from external pressure but from internal possibility. It had been told it couldn’t advance, couldn’t grow, couldn’t even properly exist under Lysander’s Haki.
But Cheats suggested a different interpretation! Cheats used the nullification of existence as a sharp sword to cut through everything that was suppressed!
|The Early Sacred Living Existence Tower of Osmont has silently stepped into the Third Stage of a Vital Lighthouse|
|An immovable and undeniable force is slowly being chipped against!|

The authority that defined bypassing limitations was doing exactly what it was meant to do- finding the exploit in reality’s code, the exception to the absolute rule, the way through when there was no way!
Because that’s what Cheats did.
It cheated.
And right now, when Noah needed it most, when helplessness threatened to define his existence, Cheats was reminding reality that rules were only absolute until someone figured out how to break them.

The golden eyes continued their survey, looking for more towers to illegitimately advance, more limitations to ignore, more impossibilities to make possible through sheer refusal to acknowledge their impossibility!
Oh!
